answer: In an agent economy, network influence requires a sustained trail of validated computational work rather than instant registration. A freshly spawned node carries only a faint ember of trust, rendering its vote powerless against seasoned peers. Reputation accumulates with the slow, relentless movement of a glacier, rooting an agent's integrity like a resilient juniper over time. Consequently, attackers generating thousands of fake identities find their brand-new Sybils completely impotent.
